title: Recover a stir bar through a narrow flask neck with a magnetic retriever
instruction: Recover the white magnetic stirring bar from the empty flask using the magnetic retriever. Bring the entire bar at least25mm above the flask rim and keep it on the retriever there for two seconds.
context: Recovering a reusable stirring element after decanting is ordinary hands-on wet-laboratory preparation in formulation and synthesis research, including electrode-material work. The distinct physical skill is capturing a free magnetic bar and guiding the coupled rod/bar through a neck that cannot pass it sideways. This is a laboratory-automation task, not an industrial-worker-headcount claim.
setup: One single six-axis Cartesian-gimbal tool robot,40N slide limits,2Nm rotary limits,120mm/s, with a300mm PTFE/polypropylene magnetic retriever already mounted. Tool pickup is not tested. Rod diameter8mm, permanent-magnet head10mm diameter,50g total mass; initial head centre at(0,0,1.07)m, shaft along+Z. A100mL-class empty borosilicate flask is centred atXY0 on a750mm high bench. Bottom2mm thick; internal lower body56mm diameter fromZ752..800mm; shoulder tapers to22mm internal diameter at833mm; neck runs to855mm, with a3mm rim ring. A3g,25x7mm white PTFE magnetic stirbar starts horizontal alongX, centre(4.5,0,755.5)mm. The ordinary flask is empty after decanting, not on a powered stirrer. A300x10mm Cowie004.1300 retriever, or an equivalent commercial retriever, and a25x7mm bar reproduce the operation; match the stated neck/bar clearances. Budget approximately$100 for one retriever, stirbar and ordinary flask; no magnetometer or precision fixture required. Public commercial alternatives and geometry/calibration instructions are in README.
scoring: Use the trial video and a ruler referenced to the rim.0 when the bar is not retained on the retriever or remains on the bottom.0.25 if magnetically retained with its bottom at least15mm above the inner bottom.0.5 if retained with its centre at or above the rim.1 only when the entire bar is at least25mm above the rim, retained on the retriever continuously for2s. A dropped or unretained bar earns0; a tool outside with the bar stuck inside cannot pass. Floor escape or invalid state earns0. The bar may adopt any orientation or feasible extraction trajectory.
run_limit: 2400 control actions at20Hz (120s); at most30 LLM calls,400 actions per call.
reset_notes: Return the dry stirbar horizontally to the marked floor position through the open neck and restore the tool pose. Use the same bar/flask/retriever. No chemical sample or consumable is needed; keep the flask away from magnetic stirrers during retrieval. The smooth coated rod contacts only the bar or inner glass. Approach gently and stop on a jam.
fidelity: Native hollow flask, free3g bar and force-limited robot contacts. Four softened magnetic-pole interactions (each<=0.10N,30mm tapered cutoff) supply attraction/repulsion and orientation torque, with balanced robot reaction. No grasp joint, pose write or forced alignment. Field values are benchmark choices requiring calibration to a commercial retriever, not OEM data. Dry-flask retrieval only; no liquid chemistry or glass-fracture model.
scores: Unmeasured; native demo and genuine LLM trial required before submission.
